reading.body:
Reid Hoffman has positioned himself across the full cycle of AI capital formation, from early backing of OpenAI in 2015 through founding a competing AI company in 2022, while maintaining influence as a venture investor at Greylock since 2009.

His trajectory shows a pattern common among technology investors: build a large-scale platform, translate that success into venture capital authority, then deploy that authority into the next wave of technology. LinkedIn's billion-member network gave Hoffman both capital and credibility. Greylock formalized his role as a backer of early-stage companies. His presence in OpenAI's founding announcement in December 2015 placed him at the moment the modern AI race began.

The data reveals a deliberate move toward concentration of influence. Hoffman joined OpenAI's board in 2018 and remained there until March 2023, when he resigned citing conflicts among his AI-related investments and roles. Within a year of that resignation, the conflict became concrete: he had co-founded Inflection AI in March 2022, months before leaving OpenAI's board. This sequence shows how a single investor can fund and direct multiple AI companies simultaneously, and why he felt compelled to step back from OpenAI governance to do so.

What this does not reveal is the scale of capital deployed, the computational resources Inflection AI commands, or how Hoffman's Greylock investments intersect with the power and infrastructure constraints that govern AI scaling. His influence is documented as organizational and financial, not as direct access to the buildings and electricity that compute requires.

standing.watch: What is unresolved according to the records is the set of filed cases involving OpenAI and Anthropic, all of which show only filing and active docket monitoring with no development recorded. The cases include TradeSun, Inc. v. OpenAI OpCo, LLC; Bass v. OpenAI, LLC; United States v. OpenAI OpCo LLC; Buist v. Anthropic, PBC; JIANG v. OPENAI GROUP PBC; Smigelski v. OpenAI OpCo, LLC; GRANT v. OPENAI INC; and Vredenburgh v. OpenAI OpCo, LLC. None of these records name Hoffman as a party, so his next steps are not set out in the records beyond his roles at Inflection AI and Greylock.
standing.record: The site's records list four companies for Hoffman: Greylock Partners, where he is an executive; Inflection AI, which he founded; LinkedIn, which he founded; and OpenAI, in which he invested. The lawsuits on the site name OpenAI entities and Anthropic, not Hoffman personally, and none record a development beyond filing and active docket monitoring. The pattern is a career built on founding and backing companies, with the legal exposure sitting at the OpenAI and Anthropic corporate level rather than with him. The records are thin on his current operational role at Inflection AI and on the outcome of any matter.
standing.standing: Reid Hoffman stands in artificial intelligence as a co-founder of Inflection AI and a partner at Greylock Partners, with a past board seat at OpenAI that ended in March 2023. The records show he co-founded LinkedIn in 2002 and became a Greylock partner in 2009. He was named as a financial backer in OpenAI's December 2015 founding announcement, joined OpenAI's board in 2018, and resigned in March 2023. He co-founded Inflection AI in 2022 with Mustafa Suleyman and Karen Simonyan. His current influence rests on Inflection AI and Greylock, while his OpenAI role is historical.
